headlines.description: Nine people were wounded during a shooting on Saturday night at a concert linked to a gang, the Tulare County Sheriff’s Office confirmed. According to a statement, shortly before 7:40 p.m., officers responded to the 20000 block of Road 256 in Strathmore, following a call about a shooting at a large party. Upon arrival, they discovered that it was a large-scale concert linked to a gang, attended by more than 150 people. According to initial reports, the suspects opened fire into the crowd, hitting at least nine people. Upon arrival, the officers immediately began providing first aid to the victims, while other individuals made their own way to local hospitals to receive medical attention. What is the connection between the shooting and gangs? Detectives determined that the event was a large-scale concert linked to a gang, featuring multiple rappers and performers, some of whom had traveled from outside the area and other states. Investigators believe the shooting could be linked to gang activity. Additionally, it was noted that, prior to the event, advertisements and promotional flyers for the concert were circulating on social media. What is the health status of the victims? Of the nine victims, a 26-year-old man was shot in the chest and requires surgery; he is in critical condition. Another man, 19 years old, was shot in the abdomen and also requires surgery. A third victim, 22 years old, was shot in the groin and requires surgery. The other six victims sustained gunshot wounds to various parts of their bodies but did not require surgery. Sheriff Boudreaux wishes to assure the public that there is no immediate threat to the residents of Tulare County.
headlines.source: Ali Thanawalla, Angelina Martin, Taylor Wirth, Kevin Topley, Dylan Grausz, Jennifer Lee Chan and Matt Maiocco
